name: Montana
overview: Montana does not auction tax liens. If property taxes are still delinquent, the county treasurer attaches a tax lien to the parcel no later than the first working day in August, and the county holds it. Investors can then take an assignment of that lien from the county treasurer by paying the delinquent taxes, penalty, interest and costs after sending the owner a certified notice; when more than one person wants the same lien, each county treasurer's own policy decides (most large counties use a lottery). Delinquent taxes carry a 2% penalty and interest of 5/6 of 1% a month. The owner can redeem until the first working day in August three years after the lien attached (two years for certain vacant subdivided lots), after which the assignee may seek a tax deed.

counties.how_to_bid: This is not a bidding auction: investors take an assignment of the county's tax lien by paying the delinquent taxes, penalty, interest and costs, and when several want the same parcel the county sets the order by lottery. counties.how_to_bid: This is not a bidding auction: investors take an assignment of the county's tax lien by paying the delinquent taxes, penalty, interest and costs, and when several want the same parcel the county sets the order by lottery. Investors mail the owner a certified Notice of Pending Assignment (from August 15, at least two weeks and not more than 60 days before payment), then submit a ranked parcel list with payment by email to treasurer@gallatin.mt.gov or by delivery to the office. Gallatin's assignment fee is $60 per parcel plus taxes, penalty and interest. Electronic submissions get first priority; within each group the program assigns each investor a random priority and selections go in snake-draft order. Complete submissions must arrive by noon on the last working day before the sale date.

counties.how_to_bid: This is not a bidding auction: investors take an assignment of the county's tax lien by paying the delinquent taxes, penalty, interest and costs, and when several want the same parcel the county sets the order by lottery. Liens attach on the first working day of August. Investors mail a Notice of Pending Assignment postmarked August 15 to owners of parcels still delinquent, then deliver receipts, notice copies, payment and an Excel assignment form by noon, August 28th. The assignment fee is $50.00 each. A lottery program sets the order (snake method, one lien per round from each buyer's list); buyers attend in person. Parcels left after the lottery can be bought first come, first served.

counties.how_to_bid: County-held tax liens can be bought by assignment in person or by mail. Counter customers are served first come, first served; duplicate mailed payments go to the earliest postage date, and a random drawing decides matching postmarks. All paperwork must be in the Treasurer's office before an assignment is issued. Contact the office before sending the two-week notice the law requires to the property owner. The county advises using an attorney if you are unfamiliar with Montana law. Fees, interest and payment methods are not stated.
